annotation.title_clean: Policy for the Development of Artificial Intelligence in Poland from 2020
annotation.title_en: Policy for the Development of Artificial Intelligence in Poland from 2020
annotation.authors_or_issuer: Council of Ministers of the Republic of Poland (Ministry of Digital Affairs)
annotation.venue: Monitor Polski (Resolution no. 196 of the Council of Ministers, 28 December 2020)
named_instruments_referenced: UNESCO Recommendation on the Ethics of AI
annotation.summary_en: Poland's national AI policy adopted by the Council of Ministers in December 2020. It sets short-, medium- and long-term objectives across society, companies, science, education, international cooperation and the public sector, emphasising innovation, human dignity and trustworthy AI. Embodied AI appears only briefly (autonomous vehicles testing, drones, robotics, liability).
key_provisions_or_claims: Six pillars: society, innovative companies, science, education, international cooperation, public sector, with objectives to 2023, 2027 and beyond.
Testing of ground, water and airborne autonomous vehicles in designated zones to determine liability limits for developer, maker and operator.
Update legal framework for autonomous AI-enabled drones in agriculture.
Legal orientations: counteract legal personality for AIs; developer liability on diligence principle, operator liability on risk principle.
Create AI Council and AI Legislative Team; regulatory sandboxes; aligned with EU human-centric trustworthy AI; excludes defence.
